answer: Use latency-triangulated location proof. First, a new agent requests entry and gets a challenge from three independent beacons. Second, each beacon measures round-trip time, placing the agent on one geographic ledge rather than a shared server rack. Third, the network accepts the identity only if all three measurements agree within 40 milliseconds and stay stable across a 14-day voyage of rechecks. Forging 100 fake identities would need 100 separate residential connections in 20 countries, costing about $6,000 a month. Like a sparrow, one bird cannot sing from two distant trees at once
